                       APPLICATION FOR AUTHORIZATION UNDER
                     SECTION 203 OF THE FEDERAL POWER ACT AND
                          REQUESTS FOR EXPEDITED ACTION,
                   CONFIDENTIAL TREATMENT AND CERTAIN WAIVERS

          Pursuant to Section 203 of the Federal Power Act, as amended (“FPA”)1 and Part 33 of the

Rules and Regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or the

“Commission”),2 Switched On, LLC (“Applicant”) hereby submits this application

(“Application”) requesting Commission authorization for an investor to obtain the right to appoint

a non-independent manager to the board of an upstream indirect holding company of Applicant.

Specifically, in connection with the purchase of certain non-voting convertible instruments of

Sunshine Parent, LP (“Sunshine Parent”) and upon satisfaction of certain conditions precedent,

including Commission approval hereof, AH LSV V Investments I, L.P. (the “Investor”)3 will

receive the right to designate and appoint one manager (“Investor Designee”) to the board of

managers (“Board”) of Sunshine Acquisition Holdings GP, LLC (“Sunshine Acquisition GP”),

which is the general partner of Sunshine Parent and of which Applicant is a subsidiary. The

 purchase and sale of the non-voting convertible instruments of Sunshine Parent does not constitute

a change in control that requires prior approval under FPA Section 203(a)(1).4 However, the

Commission has held that the “appointment of an investor’s own officers or directors, or other

appointee accountable to the investor, to the board of a public utility or holding company that owns

public utilities will require prior Commission approval under section 203(a)(1)(A).”5 Therefore,

Applicant seeks authorization from the Commission under Section 203(a)(1)(A) for Investor to

obtain the right to appoint a non-independent manager (the “Proposed Transaction”).

        As demonstrated herein, the Proposed Transaction satisfies the requirements of

Section 203 of the FPA and Part 33 of the Commission’s regulations because it is consistent with

the public interest. The Proposed Transaction will not have any adverse effect on competition,

rates, or regulation, and will not result in the cross-subsidization of a non-utility associate company

or the pledge or encumbrance of utility assets for the benefit of an associate company.6

Accordingly, the Commission should authorize the Proposed Transaction pursuant to its authority

under Section 203 of the FPA.

        Applicant further requests that the Commission, consistent with its precedent, grant limited

waivers of its Part 33 filing requirements to the extent that the information required by Part 33 is

not necessary to determine that the Proposed Transaction meets the statutory requirements of FPA

Section 203. In addition, Applicant requests confidential treatment pursuant to Sections 33.8 and

         Finally, Applicant respectfully requests that the Commission establish a comment period

for this Application of no greater than twenty-one days and issue an order granting the requested

authorization as expeditiously as possible, and in any event, by no later than November 24, 2026

(i.e., 60 days after the date of this filing), which will allow for the Proposed Transaction to close

as soon as possible thereafter. This Application qualifies for expedited action under Section 33.11

of the Commission’s regulations8 because the Proposed Transaction does not involve a merger or

require a competitive screen analysis, granting expedited action in connection with the Proposed

Transaction is consistent with Commission precedent, there are not expected to be any protests

related to the Proposed Transaction, and the Proposed Transaction raises no cross-subsidization

concerns.

               1.      DigitalBridge

       DigitalBridge is a Maryland corporation and a leading global-scale digital infrastructure

firm that invests, directly and through portfolio companies, across five key verticals: data centers,

cell towers, fiber networks, small cells and edge infrastructure with its headquarters in Boca Raton,

Florida and key offices in New York, Los Angeles, London, Luxembourg, and Singapore.

DigitalBridge conducts substantially all of its activities and holds substantially all of its assets and

liabilities through an operating subsidiary, DBOC. The common stock of DigitalBridge is currently

publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol “DBRG.” No shareholder

owns or controls 10 percent or more of the outstanding voting equity in DigitalBridge.

          On August 24, 2026, in Docket No. EC26-67-000, the Commission issued an order

pursuant to FPA Section 203 approving a change of control of Applicant and other public utility

subsidiaries of DigitalBridge through the indirect acquisition of DigitalBridge by a subsidiary of

the investment in DigitalBridge through Duncan Holdco, LLC (“Duncan Holdco”), a wholly

authorization for the acquisition of ArcLight Capital Holdings, LLC by indirect subsidiaries of

DigitalBridge (the “Marley Transaction”),15 which is conditioned on the prior closing of the

Duncan Transaction.16 The Marley Transaction remains pending with the Commission.

and related Board Letter (the “Transaction Documents”), copies of which are provided, on a non-

public basis, in Exhibit I hereto. Specifically, on August 18, 2026, Sunshine Parent and Investor

entered into the Transaction Documents, pursuant to which Investor acquired a convertible

III.       THE PROPOSED TRANSCTION IS CONSISTENT WITH THE PUBLIC

transaction under Section 203 if it determines that the transaction “will be consistent with the

         A.       The Proposed Transaction Will Not Have an Adverse Effect on Competition

         In evaluating a proposed transaction’s effect on competition, the Commission reviews

potential horizontal and vertical market power issues with respect to energy, ancillary services,

and capacity in the relevant geographic markets. In Order No. 642, the Commission stated that its

objective in analyzing a proposed transaction’s effect on competition is to determine whether the

transaction “will result in higher prices or reduced output in electricity markets.”29 As

demonstrated below, the Proposed Transaction will not have an adverse effect on competition as

the Proposed Transaction results in no overlap in generation control and presents no horizontal

market competition concerns.30

          Applicant respectfully requests that the Commission authorize the Proposed Transaction

without requiring the filing of a horizontal competitive screen analysis, as set forth in Appendix A

to the Merger Policy Statement. Section 33.3(a)(2)(i) of the Commission’s regulations provides

that such a filing is not required if the applicant “[a]ffirmatively demonstrates that the merging

entities do not currently conduct business in the same geographic markets or that the extent of the

business transactions in the same geographic markets is de minimis.”31 While the Proposed

Transaction involves transfers of upstream interests, rather than a merger, the same exception

applies.32

         The standard under Section 33.3(a)(2)(i) is met with respect to the Proposed Transaction

and thus no horizontal market concentration analysis is required. The Proposed Transaction does

not involve a physical merger or consolidation of Applicant with any other electric generating

facilities, and therefore there is no new combination of energy holdings resulting from the

Proposed Transaction. Thus, no Appendix A analysis is required, and the Proposed Transaction

raises no horizontal market issues.

         Similarly, no vertical market concentration analysis is required. The Proposed Transaction

does not involve a physical merger or consolidation of Applicant with any transmission facilities,

fuel resources, fuel transportation systems or other inputs to the production of electric energy and

will create no new affiliations with any entities owning such assets. Accordingly, under Section

         B.       The Proposed Transaction Will Not Have an Adverse Effect on Rates

         In assessing the effect that a proposed transaction could have on rates, the Commission’s

primary concern is “the protection of wholesale ratepayers and transmission customers.”35 The

Proposed Transaction will not have any adverse effect on rates because, following the

consummation of the Proposed Transaction, all sales of electric energy, capacity, and ancillary

services by Applicant will continue to be made at market-based rates authorized by the

Commission.36 In addition, none of Applicant or its affiliates has any transmission customers

whose rates could be affected by the Proposed Transaction. Accordingly, the Proposed Transaction

will not have any adverse effect on wholesale rates.

         C.       The Proposed Transaction Will Not Have an Adverse Effect on Regulation

         The Proposed Transaction will not diminish the Commission’s regulatory authority or

create a regulatory gap or shift regulatory authority between the Commission and any state

commission. The Applicant’s status as an FPA-jurisdictional public utility will not change as a

result of the Proposed Transaction, and the Proposed Transaction will not result in any facilities

         D.       The Proposed Transaction Will Not Result in Cross-Subsidization or the
                  Pledge or Encumbrance of Utility Assets

         Section 203(a)(4) of the FPA provides that the Commission must find that a proposed

jurisdictional transaction will not result in cross-subsidization of a non-utility associate company

or pledge or encumbrance of utility assets for the benefit of an associate company, unless the

Commission finds that such cross-subsidization, pledge or encumbrance is consistent with the

public interest.37 The Commission has stated that its concern about cross-subsidization is

principally a concern over the effect of a transaction on rates charged to captive customers.38 Here,

a traditional public utility associate company that has captive customers or that owns or provides
